subject: physics
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: The photoelectric effect is the emission of electrons from a metal surface when it is illuminated by light of:
questions.explain: Electrons are emitted only above a threshold frequency, evidence that light is quantised.

questions.q: The energy of a photon is given by:
questions.explain: Photon energy = Planck's constant x frequency; higher frequency means more energetic photons.

questions.q: Increasing the frequency of light in the photoelectric effect increases the:
options: Maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons
questions.explain: Higher-frequency photons carry more energy, giving emitted electrons more kinetic energy.

questions.q: The work function of a metal is the:
options: Minimum energy needed to remove an electron from the surface
questions.explain: Photon energy above the work function becomes the electron's kinetic energy (Einstein's photoelectric equation).

questions.q: Below the threshold frequency, increasing the intensity (brightness) of the light causes:
questions.explain: If each photon lacks enough energy, no electrons are emitted no matter how intense the light.

questions.q: The photoelectric effect provides evidence that light behaves as:
questions.explain: The instantaneous, frequency-dependent emission cannot be explained by the wave model alone.

questions.q: Above the threshold frequency, increasing the intensity of the light increases the:
options: Number of electrons emitted per second
questions.explain: Greater intensity means more photons per second, so more electrons are emitted, but each electron's energy is unchanged.

questions.q: Einstein's photoelectric equation is:
options: E(photon) = work function + max KE of electron
questions.explain: hf = phi + KE(max); the photon energy is shared between escaping and kinetic energy.

questions.q: Wave-particle duality is the idea that:
options: Matter and radiation can show both wave and particle behaviour
questions.explain: Light shows interference (wave) and the photoelectric effect (particle); electrons show both too.

questions.q: The de Broglie wavelength of a particle is given by:
questions.explain: A particle of momentum p has an associated wavelength h/p, significant for tiny particles like electrons.

questions.q: Electron diffraction provides evidence that electrons:
questions.explain: Electrons diffract like waves, confirming de Broglie's hypothesis of matter waves.

questions.q: The existence of discrete atomic emission spectra is evidence that electrons in atoms have:
questions.explain: Transitions between fixed energy levels produce photons of specific energies and hence discrete spectral lines.

questions.q: A photon is emitted when an electron in an atom:
options: Falls from a higher to a lower energy level
questions.explain: The photon's energy equals the difference between the two levels (E = hf).

questions.q: Higher-frequency photons (e.g. ultraviolet vs infrared) carry:
questions.explain: Since E = hf, energy increases with frequency.

questions.q: The threshold frequency of a metal depends on its:
questions.explain: A larger work function requires a higher threshold frequency for emission.

questions.q: Planck's constant h relates a photon's energy to its:
questions.explain: E = hf links energy and frequency via Planck's constant.

questions.q: In the photoelectric effect, electrons are emitted almost instantly above the threshold frequency, which supports:
options: The particle (photon) model, as one photon gives its energy to one electron
A time delay for energy build-up
questions.explain: Instant emission contradicts the wave prediction of a gradual energy build-up.

questions.q: Matter waves (de Broglie) are significant for electrons but not for everyday objects because:
options: Large objects have very large momentum, giving a negligibly small wavelength
questions.explain: lambda = h/p is immeasurably tiny for macroscopic objects, so wave effects are unobservable.

questions.q: If the frequency of incident light is doubled (well above threshold), the maximum kinetic energy of emitted electrons:
questions.explain: More energetic photons leave more energy as electron kinetic energy after overcoming the work function.

questions.q: The quantisation of energy means energy is:
options: Transferred in discrete packets (quanta) rather than continuously
questions.explain: Quantum theory describes energy exchange in fixed amounts (quanta), such as photons.
